Guard rules for dsh-living-memory — a GENERIC MINIMAL set, shipped on purpose.
Load order: (1) ~/.dsh/dsh-living-memory/guard-rules.json  (2) this file  (3) the built-in GUARD_FLOOR in index.cjs.
Whichever of (1)/(2) is read first wins AS A WHOLE; GUARD_FLOOR's reject rules are always appended and cannot be turned off.

Why minimal: a content-safety word list IS the defense — publishing an exhaustive one lets anyone compute exactly what slips through. So this file ships only broadly applicable credential / prompt-injection / encoded-payload shapes, and leaves two things to you:
  - provider-specific key shapes (e.g. a 32-hex-dot-16 token) — add them to your own rules file;
  - domain vocabulary for the sensitive-topic gate and the single-subject wording gate — both are empty/generic here.
singleBodyWarn is EMPTY in the public build, which disables that gate by construction (the code path stays intact).

Keep the (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) prefix boundary when adding credential prefixes: without it, file names like `…yml.bak-20260827`, `task-…`, `disk-…` get caught by the `ak-`/`sk-` substring.

reject._note: long single-segment key with a known prefix family (sk/pk/ak/ark)
multi-segment key (prefix-shortpart.sep.sep…), which a plain {16,} character class misses
assignment form. Known trade-off: prose that DISCUSSES such an assignment can trip it
